beats.text: The villain? The reward model. It acts as a bloated middleman. Us to sample. Score. And optimize in a fragile. Multi-stage dance.
beats.visual_focus: A heavy, clunky gear labeled 'Reward Model' grinding against a smooth gear labeled 'Policy'.

beats.text: Direct Preference Optimization cuts the middleman. We map human preferences directly to the model's log-probabilities. Reinforcement learning into simple classification.
beats.visual_focus: A direct, straight line replacing a complex, winding path.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: Finally, a script that doesn't treat me like a toddler. The hook actually hits a pain point—everyone knows RLHF is a nightmare to tune—so I stayed. You explained the 'why' (getting rid of the reward model) and the 'how' (mapping preferences to log-probs) without using any of that 'digital brain' or 'smart assistant' cringe. It’s technical, fast, and actually makes sense.
